messages.author: 89a4640ddc6e46d0
messages.subject: Invalid Covariance Matrix
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to conduct a multivariate meta-analysis for a temporal outcome. I have standard deviations and number of subject at various time points. But these data are missing for many observations. I also do not know the covariance or correlation matrix. I am treating missing observations (standard deviation and N) as parameters, and the correlation matrix as a parameter. My full model with data is available here: https://drive.google.com/folderview?id=0B2_rKFnvrjMAZkZ2aGRXZlBiRUU&usp=sharing

The crux of my problem I believe is here:

(...)
parameters{
  real <lower=0> sig_ms[len_sig_ms]; #missing standard deviations
  real <lower=1> N_ms[len_N_ms]; #missing N
  corr_matrix [Ntm] Rhomat;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector <lower=0> [Ntm] sig [Nobs];
  vector <lower=1> [Ntm] N [Nobs];
  matrix [Ntm,Ntm] Vmat [Nobs];
  cov_matrix [Ntm] SIGMA [Nobs];
 
(...) #data and parameters for observed and missing are combined in transformed parameter
     
   for (obs in 1:Nobs){
    for (m in 1:Ntm){
      SIGMA[obs,m,m] <- sig[obs,m] * sig[obs,m]  / N[obs,m];
    }
    for (m in 1:(Ntm-1)) {
      for (n in (m+1):Ntm) {
        SIGMA[obs,m,n] <- sig[obs,m]/sqrt(N[obs,m]) * sig[obs,n]/sqrt(N[obs,m])*Rhomat[m,n];
        SIGMA[obs,n,m] <- SIGMA[obs,m,n];
      }
    }
  }
}
model{
  Rhomat ~ lkj_corr(1);
  sig_ms~cauchy(0,2.5); #missing standard deviations
}


I get the following error:
Invalid value of SIGMA: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: SIGMA[k0__]SIGMA[k0__] is not positive definite. SIGMA[k0__](0,0) is 6.398872095158112e-008:0.Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.
Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.


I'm not sure why I am getting this error. From the manual, I believe I am correctly parametrizing the correlation matrix (Rhomat). I think the missing standard deviation and N are appropriately constrained.

was hoping for some pointers...

thanks

mark

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Invalid Covariance Matrix
parts:
I would start by taking SIGMA out of the transformed parameters block and put it into the model block. That way, it is not checked for positive-definiteness which you know holds by construction but possibly not numerically. Also, comment out the

rhomat ~ lkj_corr(1);

line because all that does is check for positive-definiteness of rhomat, since any valid rhomat has the same density.

If that is insufficient, then there may be deeper problems, and you might have to go to Cholesky factors as parameters, which is actually where everyone should be starting from these days.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Invalid Covariance Matrix
parts:
On Friday, September 19, 2014 2:45:27 PM UTC-4, Markian Pahuta wrote:
I get the error

integer parameters or transformed parameters are not allowed;  found declared type int, parameter name=N_ms Problem with declaration.

How can I sample from the poisson distribution to impute?

You could put a poisson_rng statement into the generated quantities block to impute under missing-at-random assumptions, but you can't declare integer-valued unknowns in the parameters block.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Invalid Covariance Matrix
parts:
You can't use something from the generated quantities block in the transformed parameters block, in part because the stuff in generated quantities is executed after the sampling is finished. There are some functions in Stan that will automatically coerce integers to real numbers when appropriate, but it would not be appropriate in other circumstances, so there is no function for doing so.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Invalid Covariance Matrix
parts:
Markian asked about converting integer to real, and
if that's the intent, then it's automatic. Just like
in C++ or Java --- you can use an integer where you can
use a real. For example:

y ~ normal(0, 1);

the 0 and 1 are integers and normal takes (real,real) arguments.
You can also do this:

real z;
int n;
n <- 3;
z <- n;

- Bob
